Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

wonderful adjective

marvellous, delightful

also marvellous, marvelous, amazing (very good), wonderfully, splendid, admirable, fantastic, awesome!, awesome

classical

Cic. Att. 4.11.2: cum homine mīrificō … Dionȳsiō
Cic. Fam. 3.11.4: mīrificamque cēpī voluptātem
Traupman 147, 152: mīrifica est, she is fantastic

mīrificus, mīrifica, mīrificum

adjective · Declension on Wiktionary

wonderful, marvellous, extraordinary

The warm word of Cicero’s letters, of people and things alike; the adverb mīrificē, wonderfully, is even commoner there. Literally “causing wonder”, so it can also mean strange, extraordinary (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • praeclārus, praeclāra, praeclārum — splendid, excellent

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 14.20.2: Dolābellae praeclāra · Declension on Wiktionary

    Very bright, so splendid, noble, famous; praise of a deed, a speech, a book (Lewis & Short).

  • admīrābilis, admīrābile — admirable, wonderful

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 146, 159: exemplum admīrābile, a wonderful example; Traupman 149, 408 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Worth admiring; Cicero also uses it in irony: ō admīrābilem impudentiam! (Cic. Phil. 3.18, Lewis & Short).

  • mīrābilis, mīrābile — wonderful, marvellous

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 7.26.5: dictū mīrābile · Declension on Wiktionary

    Above all in mīrābile dictū, wonderful to tell; of anything that causes wonder, pleasant or not.

Examples

  • nōs hīc vorāmus litterās cum homine mīrificō (ita mē hercule sentiō) Dionȳsiō

    here we are devouring books with Dionysius, a wonderful man (I really mean it)Cic. Att. 4.11.2

  • tuumque simul prōmptum animum et alacrem perspexī ad dēfendendam rem pūblicam mīrificamque cēpī voluptātem ex hāc tuā dīligentiā

    and I saw how ready and eager you are to defend the state, and your care gave me wonderful pleasureCic. Fam. 3.11.4

  • dictū mīrābile, tenuit nōn sōlum āles captam semel sēdem

    wonderful to tell, the bird not only kept the seat it had once takenLiv. 7.26.5

  • Mīrābile!

    Awesome!Traupman 275

See also great, amaze, be surprised, nice, terrible.
